hints: Look closely at what happens to $\text{CN}^-$ at the start and at the end of the two steps shown.
Notice how $\text{CN}^-$ uses its lone pair to attack the slightly positive carbon in $\text{C=O}$ in the first step.
Count atoms going from $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{HCN}$ to the cyanohydrin product to see if anything is lost or just joined together.
walkthrough:
**Spot what CN- does**

Think of this like a helper that starts the job and gets handed back at the end. In step 1, $\text{CN}^-$ is used up, but in step 2 it is reformed.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{HCN} \xrightarrow{\text{CN}^-} \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$$

**Check for nucleophile behaviour**

A nucleophile loves positive centres and donates a pair of electrons. Here $\text{:CN}^-$ donates its lone pair to the $\delta+$ carbon of the polar $\text{C=O}$ bond.

$$\text{C}^{\delta+}=\text{O}^{\delta-} + \text{:CN}^- \rightarrow \text{C(CN)}-\text{O}^-$$

**Check for addition and catalysis**

Nothing leaves, the $\text{H}$ and $\text{CN}$ simply add across the $\text{C=O}$ double bond to give a cyanohydrin. Because $\text{CN}^-$ is regenerated unchanged, it fits the definition of a catalyst.

So statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.

options.A: Correct. Statement 1 is true because CN- is used in step 1 and regenerated in step 2, so it is a catalyst. Statement 2 is true because CN- donates its lone pair to the electron-deficient carbonyl carbon, so it is a nucleophile. Statement 3 is true because H and CN add across C=O with no other product, so it is nucleophilic addition.
options.B: Incorrect because it leaves out statement 3. This is the trap of thinking protonation is substitution. The overall change joins HCN across the C=O bond to form $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$ with no by-product, which is clearly addition.
options.C: Incorrect because it leaves out statement 1. Students sometimes miss that a reactant in one step can be a catalyst if it is reformed later. Here CN- appears on the left in step 1 and on the right in step 2, unchanged overall.
options.D: Incorrect because it claims only statement 1 is correct. This misses the key ideas of the mechanism. CN- is clearly donating an electron pair to C=O, so it is nucleophilic, and the reaction is addition of HCN to an aldehyde.
